 NFL live updates: Aidan Hutchinson, Drake Maye latest, news, reaction and more from Week 10
 Follow our live coverage as we break down the aftermath of Sunday’s NFL games. Live Blog Chat The Athletic Live Team November 16, 2026 at 7:00 PM EST The Patriots expect Drake Maye to miss extended time with a knee injury, per sources.   AP Photo Lukas Weese · Staff Writer, Live NFL Week 10 reaction — Latest
 Join us as we review, analyze and discuss another compelling Sunday of NFL action. 
 Multiple reports confirm Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson is out for the season with a knee injury, while Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and Jets quarterback Geno Smith left their respective games with ankle concerns. Maye will miss extended time due to the injury, league sources told The Athletic .
 Today's news conferences and radio interviews have also provided clarity on the upcoming weeks of the season. The Packers are planning for Micah Parsons to return for their Thanksgiving Eve game, and the Seahawks will start Sam Darnold if he is healthy for their next game, which is against the 49ers.
 Follow along for all the latest news, fallout and analysis.

 Email us your thoughts: live@theathletic.com

 November 16, 2026 at 7:00 PM EST Dan Duggan · Senior Writer, Giants Giants tweak roster ahead of Week 11
 Say this for this regime, they haven’t wasted time addressing weaknesses. Charlie Jones was really shaky fielding punts, so he’s out. Xavier Gipson has 12 fumbles in 41 career games, so this may not cure the ball security concerns. 
 And the fact that they’re sticking with Dominic Zvada through his struggles tells you how much faith they have in him.

 November 16, 2026 at 6:50 PM EST The Athletic NFL Staff Exploring Klubnik's future with the Jets
 Zack Rosenblatt explains why it's fair to wonder at what point the Jets could lean into Cade Klubnik as their next starting quarterback.
 November 16, 2026 at 6:40 PM EST Mike DeFabo · Senior Writer, Steelers Anderson next in line to replace McCormick
   Getty Images Spencer Anderson appears set to be the next man up in place of Mason McCormick , at least initially.
 “This will be his opportunity,” coach Mike McCarthy said.
 McCarthy added that rookie guard Gennings Dunker will also be part of the conversation.
 November 16, 2026 at 6:30 PM EST Matt Barrows · Senior Writer, 49ers Shanahan addresses 49ers' pass-rushing lapses
   IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kyle Shanahan on the 49ers' pass rush: "I wouldn't have said it was a bad-pass-rush game by any means – if I hadn't watched the fourth quarter." 
 He said the defensive line fatigued in the fourth quarter when they allowed three straight TDs.
 November 16, 2026 at 6:20 PM EST Matt Schneidman · Staff Writer, Packers LaFleur targets Parsons' return against Rams
 Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Monday that he plans for defensive end Micah Parsons to make his season debut next Wednesday night in Los Angeles against the Rams.
 However, LaFleur smiled and said his timeline has been different than everyone else’s during Parsons’ entire rehab, implying that he planned for Parsons to be back already.
 “We’ll see,” LaFleur said of his best player. “Obviously having been in practice and banking some reps, there are still a couple more hurdles for him to clear before we can definitely say that he’s a go. But he’s been showing progress, and we’ll see where he’s at by the end of the week.”

 November 16, 2026 at 6:10 PM EST Matt Barrows · Senior Writer, 49ers Shanahan optimistic on Evans' outlook
   Getty Images Mike Evans and other rehabbing 49ers will fly into Colorado Springs today. Shanahan would only go so far to say he's "hoping" Evans can rejoin the team at practice this week.
 November 16, 2026 at 6:00 PM EST Joseph Person · Senior Writer, Panthers Panthers sign Marco Wilson
   Getty Images The Carolina Panthers announced they have signed cornerback Marco Wilson to the active roster after exhausting his practice squad elevations. In a corresponding move, Carolina waived outside linebacker Nick Hampton .
 November 16, 2026 at 5:50 PM EST James Boyd · Staff Writer, Colts Colts' Gardner may not play on Thursday
   Getty Images Colts coach Shane Steichen confirmed that CB Sauce Gardner suffered a left calf injury yesterday. This is his third left calf injury since joining the Colts via trade last year.
 Gardner is TBD in terms of playing Thursday night against the Houston Texans. The same goes for fellow starting cornerbac Charvarius Ward Sr. (shin injury).
 November 16, 2026 at 5:40 PM EST James Boyd · Staff Writer, Colts Steichen sticking with Daniel Jones
   Getty Images Colts HC Shane Steichen continues to dismiss the idea of potentially benching Daniel Jones , despite his poor play.
 It doesn’t make any sense.
 GO FURTHER
 Colts coach Shane Steichen running out of ways to defend the indefensible: Daniel Jones
 November 16, 2026 at 5:30 PM EST Matt Schneidman · Staff Writer, Packers LaFleur details issues with pass protection
 A couple things Matt LaFleur said about the pass pro today:
 Thought they could have long-developing plays early and protection didn't hold up
 Still struggled when Packers blockers outnumbered Vikings rushers, losing 1-on-1s
 "Big problem" that chippers sometimes didn't touch guys
 Vikings timed cadences, Packers changed them up but need more urgency in and out of huddle so not snapping the ball with 2/3 secs left
 Too many free runners and both schematic and execution problems

 November 16, 2026 at 5:20 PM EST Doug Haller · Senior Writer, Arizona Assessing Carson Beck’s first NFL start
 Carson Beck’s first NFL start did not go well. The Cardinals offense went nowhere. His numbers were terrible.
 One play offered hope. 
 November 16, 2026 at 5:10 PM EST Nicki Jhabvala · Senior Writer, Washington Commanders Quinn shares update on Tunsil's status
   Getty Images Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Laremy Tunsil has progressed to the next phase of his recovery. Still too early to say if he'll be able to return this season.
 November 16, 2026 at 5:00 PM EST Andrew Destin · Staff Writer, Seahawks Darnold remains Seahawks' starter
   Getty Images Seattle Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald confirmed Monday that Sam Darnold will start at quarterback against the San Francisco 49ers on Nov. 29, provided he is healthy enough to play.
 “Sam’s our starting quarterback,” Macdonald said during his weekly radio appearance on Seattle Sports 710. “I can’t wait for him to be fully healthy, probably for the first time — minimal times it’s happened this year.” 
 November 16, 2026 at 4:50 PM EST Zach Berman · Senior Writer, Eagles Eagles bring back T.J. Paganetti as consultant
 The Philadelphia Eagles are hiring T.J. Paganetti in a consulting role, according to a league source, as first reported by ESPN.
 Paganetti, who was fired earlier this month as the New Orleans Saints' run game coordinator, previously spent 12 seasons with Philadelphia from 2013 to 2024 before following Kellen Moore to New Orleans.
 He served as the Eagles' assistant offensive line coach and run game specialist during their Super Bowl-winning 2024 season.
 His consulting role will be similar to those held by Marcus Brady and Jim Bob Cooter, who contributed to Philadelphia's coaching staff in recent years.
 November 16, 2026 at 4:40 PM EST Sam Warren · Staff Writer, Raiders Raiders' Bowers (ankle) ruled day-to-day
   Getty Images Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said star tight end Brock Bowers is day-to-day with his ankle injury.
 “It’s not as bad as we thought, but still a significant injury.” 
 Bowers went to the medical tent early in the Raiders’ loss to the Seahawks on Sunday, then briefly returned to the game before exiting with the ankle injury.

 November 16, 2026 at 4:30 PM EST James Boyd · Staff Writer, Colts Steichen addresses relationship with Jones
   Getty Images Colts HC Shane Steichen , asked if he treats QB Daniel Jones different than others on the team:
 “I treat all of my players the same. Obviously, the QB is different, no matter who the starting QB is. … But I do treat all the players the same.” 
 On if his handling of Jones contradicts his message of accountability:
 “I have those conversations with (DJ). Obviously, I have game reviews on Monday and show the clips where we all gotta be better. And that’s not just him. …” 
 November 16, 2026 at 4:20 PM EST Zac Jackson · Staff Writer, Browns Monken noncommittal on Watson's future
   Getty Images Todd Monken said he has not talked to Andrew Berry about Deshaun Watson ’s future past this season – and later said that goes for the whole roster. 
 “I’m not really in any position to talk about any of our players. We have seven games left … I’m worried about walkthrough tomorrow.” 
 November 16, 2026 at 4:10 PM EST John Riker · Staff Writer, Live NFC South is wide open
   Getty Images Yesterday's clash between the Panthers and Saints determined which team would be the leader of the division. Ultimately, Carolina pulled out the road win in a game that featured multiple field goals in the final minute of regulation. 
 The Panthers' win hardly wraps up the race. Currently, Carolina boasts four wins and the other three teams in the division have three wins, so any team could make a run at the division over the next month.
 The Athletic 's NFL playoff projection model views the NFC South as the league's most competitive division, with no team having more than a 50 percent chance of winning the division. The 3-6 Buccaneers are the model's favorite at 45, with the Panthers just behind at 32 percent. The Falcons and Saints linger behind at 14 and 9 percent, respectively. And given the success of the NFC North and West teams, the model does not envision any of the four teams capturing a wild-card spot.
 Tampa Bay has the best defense in the NFL by TruMedia's defensive EPA/play (0.18) and has the 12th-ranked offensive EPA/rush (-0.04), but the quarterback position is a major question mark. The Panthers have the best offense and the lead in the standings. And the Falcons and Saints have flashed signs of competitiveness against top teams in the league. This race won't produce a Super Bowl contender, but it should be dramatic once again.
 November 16, 2026 at 4:00 PM EST Paul Dehner Jr. · Senior Writer, Bengals Taylor switched up his coin-toss approach
   IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect For the first time this year, Zac Taylor won the toss and opted to receive. Choosing to weaponize his offense to set the tone. 
 When did he know he would take that approach against Pittsburgh?
 "I think I texted Joe Monday morning at 8 am."
